info.title: Not measurable on this ledger:
info.body: OTIF (on-time in-full delivery), lead-time reliability, purchase-price variance and maverick (off-PO) spend all require purchase-order → receipt → bill line linkage, which this data does not carry (no document links, no line-level items on bills). Payment behavior, concentration and relationship scorecards are computed from complete data.

analysis.rsfNote: = amount ÷ the vendor's historical 2nd-largest transaction (36-month baseline, computed in one window-function pass). RSF ≥ 10 means a transaction wildly out of scale for that vendor — a classic error/fraud signal.
analysis.zscoreNote: measures how many standard deviations a transaction sits from that vendor's own average (per-vendor baselines over 36 months, one aggregate pass). |z| ≥ 3 flags entity-specific outliers that global thresholds miss.

sequential.indicatorNote1: if a vendor's invoice numbers to you are perfectly sequential over weeks or months, you are likely their
sequential.indicatorNote2: customer. Legitimate vendors have numbering gaps from invoicing others. Detected by scanning every vendor's reference numbers for unbroken runs.

ghost.title: Ghost vendors
ghost.note: are payee companies controlled by employees. Two-phase matching across the full party registry: employee names against vendor names, and normalized street addresses (line 1 + postal code) shared between a paid vendor and an employee. Name match scores 75, shared address 90, both 95.

empty.noGhostMatches: No vendor–employee name or address matches found
empty.noAuditEvents: No high-risk audit events in this period

sentinel.auditNote: Native audit log. Most records in this ledger were bulk-migrated, so change history begins at go-live — the trail grows as users work in openbooks.
sentinel.trapNote: Amounts just below round thresholds (ending in 99, 999, or 9999) can indicate purchases engineered to stay under an approval limit. Recurrent traps from the same requester or vendor warrant review.

config.duplicatesNote: Same vendor + document kind + amount; credits excluded; confidence by memo/date proximity
config.rsfNote: Amount ÷ vendor 2nd-largest over a 36-month baseline ({floor} baseline floor)
config.zscoreNote: Per-vendor mean/σ baseline, ≥5 transactions and σ > {sigma}
config.sequentialNote: Gap-free vendor reference numbers; 30+ day spans rank high risk
config.trapNote: Whole-dollar endings (.00 or .99 cents) just under round limits
config.weekendNote: Accounting document date (migrated data carries import timestamps, so system created-time is not meaningful here)

duplicateDays.label: Duplicate window (days)
duplicateDays.help: Same vendor, kind and amount within this many days flags a pair

duplicateMinAmount.label: Duplicate minimum ($)
duplicateMinAmount.help: Pairs below this amount are ignored

sequentialMinCount.label: Sequential run minimum
sequentialMinCount.help: Gap-free invoice-number runs need at least this many documents

sequentialMinDays.label: Sequential span (days)
sequentialMinDays.help: Runs spread over fewer days are treated as batch entry, not a flag

coverage.introTail: — no 30-day windows, no per-vendor shortcuts, no sampling. Nothing is skipped:
coverage.benfordItem: — flags amounts whose leading digits don’t follow natural spending patterns.
coverage.rszItem: — compares each transaction to that vendor’s own history to surface outliers.
coverage.sequentialItem: — catches suspiciously unbroken sequences of vendor reference numbers.
coverage.duplicatesItem: — compares every pair of transactions to catch repeated or split payments.
coverage.outro: This period: {docs} documents ({amount}) across {days} days, analyzed in {seconds}s. Detail tables show the top matches per check; the counts and distributions always cover everything.
